text: Which new unit types should Milestone 3 add to today's four? Choose all that apply; leave all unticked to add none.

options.label: Artillery group
options.rationale: The arm with the clearest historical weight that fits the battle table; the owner's roll-bonus rule needs it.

options.label: Air as faction air wings (not counters)
options.rationale: Air mattered (the airlift, the Condor Legion), and abstract wings avoid crowding the map.

options.label: Cavalry (both sides fielded it; the Nationalist cavalry division charged at Alfambra in February 1938)
Tanks (T-26, Panzer I, CV-33; few and rarely decisive)
Anti-air as a unit (the 88 mm mostly served as anti-tank artillery)
Aircraft as map counters split into recon, fighter, and bomber

text: How should artillery's special effect work?

options.label: Owner's rule on the d20 scale: value counts, +1 per 3 artillery points, capped at +3, no attack by artillery alone
options.rationale: On a d20, +1 is a third of an odds column, so the rule is meaningful without counting the guns twice.

options.label: Owner's rule literally, on today's d6 (+1 per 3 points is a whole odds column)
Artillery counts as attack value only, no roll bonus
Roll bonus only; artillery adds nothing to the odds
Drop this idea or defer it

text: How should air power be represented?

options.label: Faction air wings from a scenario schedule, each assigned per turn to support a battle or to intercept; bombing cities waits (Q-UNIT-4)
options.rationale: Captures the Condor Legion and Soviet air support with one new order kind and no new counters, and keeps the economic side out until wings prove themselves.

options.label: Aircraft counters on the map with recon, fighter, and bomber roles
A fixed per-faction battle modifier from data, with no player decision
Drop this idea or defer it

text: What should bombing a town do?

options.label: Defer bombing until air wings prove themselves; when it comes, a small one-turn yield cut in one city (proposal: -25 percent)
options.rationale: The cut parks bombing for Milestone 3, and AA is deferred, so there is nothing to blunt it yet.

options.label: A small one-turn yield cut in Milestone 3 (-25 percent), with no defence
A lasting cut until the city is repaired with money
No economic effect ever; air only supports battles

text: How long should the new unit types (artillery, and later tanks or cavalry) take to train?

options.label: Per-type trainingTurns in unitTypes, on the same scale as Q-RECR-3: artillery 2 turns like the other formed types; any faster militia comes from place tags (Q-RECR-4), not faction rules
options.rationale: One training rule for every type; the owner's 'some factions recruit militia faster' is covered by places that change hands with the ground.

options.label: Longer for heavy types: artillery 3 turns, tanks 4
Every recruit arrives next turn; types differ only in cost
Drop this idea or defer it

text: How many special effects may one unit type carry?

options.label: At most one, stated in one line on the counter tooltip and named in battle breakdowns
options.rationale: Keeps 'lets not muddy this too much' enforceable and every effect visible where it fights.

options.label: Several per type, as each type needs
None; new types differ only in their attack and defence values

text: Should generals appear, and with what effect?

options.label: Display-only commander chips on factions and named armies (Franco, Mola, Rojo, Miaja), no rules effect
options.rationale: Gives players the 'Francisco commands the purple' cue at almost no rules cost.

options.label: Generals attached to armies with one small effect (e.g. +2 on the d20 once per turn)
Leader counters that limit which armies can act (Hannibal style)
Drop this idea or defer it

text: Should commanders change on historical dates?

options.label: Yes, scripted by turn in scenario data (Mola to Davila at about turn 22), display only
options.rationale: One fromTurn/untilTurn pair per commander teaches the history with no rules weight.

options.label: No, keep the 1936 commanders all game
Yes, and tie it to events such as a random chance of loss

text: Which die and result set should combat use?

options.label: d20 with an 11-grade ladder and faded losses
options.rationale: The only option that gives idea 7 a graded 'how much ground' signal while keeping today's take chance per column.

options.label: d20 with today's seven results (more granularity, data-only change)
Keep the d6 and only fade the losses
2d6 bell curve
Drop this idea or defer it

text: How many graded results should the ladder have?

options.label: 11, from attacker routed to defender destroyed, including gives ground (1 sub-region) and pushed back (2)
options.rationale: Enough to grade ground for idea 7, few enough to read in a battle report.

options.label: 9 (merge stalled with shaken, and routed with destroyed)
7, as today
13 or more

text: How should the d20 table be written in scenario data?

options.label: A ladder of grades with minimum scores plus a column step (score = clamped roll + 3 x column)
options.rationale: 11 lines of data instead of 147 cells, and it keeps today's one-step-per-column property.

options.label: An explicit 7 x 21 table like today's table[column][row]
Both: the ladder in data, expanded to a table at load for display

text: How should casualties fade?

options.label: Each grade costs a share of each army's men (10, 20, or 35 percent); outright destruction only on the top grade, surrender, or below 25 percent strength
options.rationale: Proportional and easy to explain; armies wear down instead of vanishing.

options.label: Keep today's attrition: losses worth the opposing side's value
Step losses: each army loses one or two fixed steps

text: How should demoralization fade?

options.label: Each grade demoralizes none, half, or all of a side's value, weakest armies first, as today
options.rationale: Reuses M16's existing share rule; only the share changes per grade.

options.label: Every grade that demoralizes hits every army on the side
Replace demoralization with fatigue hits on a 0-3 track

text: What happens to today's roll modifiers (works +1 to +3, Popular resistance, the below-1:1 penalty) on the d20?

options.label: Restate them in d20 units in the new ruleset's data (x3: works +3 per turn up to +9)
options.rationale: Keeps their weight; left at +1, works at +3 would drop from 50 to 15 percent of a d20.

options.label: Keep them at today's sizes, so they matter much less
Add a single modifierScale field and keep today's numbers

text: What should partial-ground grades (gives ground, pushed back) do where sub-regions do not apply?

options.label: Act as a stalemate: both lose men, no ground changes, and both bounce in head-on battles
options.rationale: Keeps the ladder valid whether or not idea 7 lands, and in M19, M20, and M27 battles.

options.label: Count them as the defender driven out
Remove them from the ladder when partitioning is off

text: How far should an army move per turn?

options.label: Keep one move per turn now; add a sub-region allowance per type only if idea 7 lands
options.rationale: Yague's columns covered about one territory per two-week turn; points only matter on a finer grid.

options.label: Movement points per type now, on today's territories
A faction-wide action point budget for moves and attacks
Drop this idea or defer it

text: How should exhaustion work?

options.label: Offensive exhaustion: attacking in N turns running demoralizes the army; one quiet turn recovers it
options.rationale: Reuses M23 morale, adds one counter and one data field, and no third value multiplier.

options.label: A fatigue track 0-3 with a value penalty at 2 and demoralization at 3
Attrition rolls for long moves or mountain crossings (Hannibal style)
Drop this idea or defer it

text: How should exhausted armies recover?

options.label: Any turn without a move order, the same trigger that already entrenches or rests (M22, M23)
options.rationale: Submissions stay lists of move orders; no new Rest order to learn.

options.label: An explicit Rest order
Only in a friendly city or a supplied territory

text: How many consecutive attack turns before an army is exhausted?

options.label: 3 turns (six weeks), as one scenario value
options.rationale: A judgement: the drive from Seville reached Talavera in about 2.3 turns (2 August to 3 September) before halting, a halt usually tied to the decision to relieve Toledo rather than exhaustion. The harness should test 2 to 4.

options.label: 2 turns
4 turns
Per unit type (e.g. colonial 4, militia 2)

text: Should defending also count toward exhaustion?

options.label: No, only attacking tires an army
options.rationale: Keeps static fronts stable and puts the cost of tempo on the attacker.

options.label: Yes, every battle fought counts
Only battles with a bad result for that army

text: Should Milestone 3 add action points (a limited number of armies that may act each turn)?

options.label: No, drop action points
options.rationale: Activation limits change the simultaneous 'every army may move' game and add a resource the owner hedged on.

options.label: Yes, a per-faction activation budget from scenario data
Yes, but only as a limit on attacks, not moves

text: With faded casualties, how should men, morale, and exhaustion combine on one army?

options.label: Men are the only lasting damage (restored by money); morale and exhaustion are temporary and recover by resting; no third value multiplier
options.rationale: Each effect has one cause and one cure, and values stay type x strength x morale as today.

options.label: Add a fatigue multiplier on top of strength and morale
Make demoralization last until the army is restored with money

text: Below what strength should a worn-down army break up?

options.label: 25 percent of fullStrength
options.rationale: Stops remnants lingering at value 1 once losses fade, and gives restore orders a deadline.

options.label: 10 percent of fullStrength
Never; only the minimum value of 1 applies, as today
